title: Arrangers for Russell, Oliver and Armstrong
summary: Who arranged for Russell, Oliver and Armstrong: Oliver wrote nothing down, and Armstrong's office hired arrangers including a white man.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: He did a lot of arrangements, you know.
Yeah.
Who else arranged for that band?
Around that time, uh... Bingham Addison? Well, Bingham Addison, you do.
Did you have many arrangers around, uh... saying King Oliver's times? Who else arranged for King Oliver other than... than Louis Russell? Or did Louis Russell arrange much for... For King Oliver?

No, well, uh... Oliver had his own ideas, I mean, what I think. I don't recall that Oliver had anything written down, I mean, it's... No, he's never writing nothing down. He never did write nothing down. I never seen no music up there. I don't remember, maybe he did, but I doubt it.
What about, uh... Louis Armstrong? Did he have any arrangers when you worked with him?

Well, yeah, he had, uh... Chapper Willett, and, well, a few others, I mean. Yeah. That Chapper Willett was one of the main arrangers. At the time I was with the big band there, wasn't out of college then.
What about Louis Russell?
Well, he's a pretty good arranger.
For Armstrong, too, he did some?
Well, he made a few introductions and things like that. I don't think he ever made a big arrangement, no. I can't recall. Nope.
Well that's funny. He would arrange for his own band, but not for Armstrong.
Well I think the office, I mean, had hired Chapper Willett to make all the arrangements. And Chapper and, it's another guy, I can't think.
What did the guy play?

No, he didn't play anything. He played the piano, I imagine, I mean, the arranger, I mean. I never heard him play nothing. But I know he used to come to that arrangement. I don't know, I can't call the guy's name. I don't think you'll find him in there.
No, a colored guy, huh?
No, a white guy.
A white guy did the arrangements.

Yeah, he made, this number we played so fast, that music, swing that music, and all, and he arranged numbers like that. Da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da. Swing that music.
Wouldn't be anybody like Bob Haggard, the bass player with Bob Crosby.
I wouldn't bother, no, I wouldn't bother. Yeah.
